avoid_months.reason: The shrines are closed for winter. They reopen around Akshaya Tritiya (April or May) and close around Diwali and Bhai Dooj (October or November). Exact dates are announced each year.

stops.name: Yamunotri Temple
stops.note: The last 5 to 6 km from Janki Chatti is a trek. Ponies and palkis are available, but many pilgrims walk.

stops.name: Gangotri Temple
stops.note: Reached directly by road via Uttarkashi.

stops.name: Kedarnath Temple
stops.note: Not reachable by road. From Gaurikund it is a 16 to 18 km uphill trek, or a helicopter booked only through IRCTC. See the separate Kedarnath card for the full rules.

stops.name: Badrinath Temple
stops.note: Opening dates are announced each year. Timings and access details could not be confirmed.

booking_notes.text: Online registration is mandatory and free for all pilgrims. Register on the Uttarakhand portal or the Tourist Care Uttarakhand app. Carry the registration slip and a valid photo ID throughout. Registration opens a few weeks before the season (in 2026 it opened on 6 March).
Helicopter tickets, especially for Kedarnath, can only be booked with valid registration, on the official IRCTC HeliYatra site. The ID used for booking must match the ID shown at boarding.

elderly_notes: Yamunotri involves a 5 to 6 km trek and Kedarnath a 16 to 18 km uphill trek at high altitude; both are hard for older pilgrims. Ponies, palkis and helicopters exist, and a doctor's advice is sensible before going. Medical checkpoints and ambulances are placed along the route.
unverified: Days are one per shrine only. Road travel days between the shrines are NOT included. News reports say the full circuit usually takes a week or more by road, so this card is incomplete for a real trip
